If you're struggling with suicidal thoughts, depression, or any other condition that's negatively affecting you, reach out. Find that compassion you need. Talk. People will listen. There will always be someone.

As someone with diagnosed, chronic depression, I can tell you that this condition is incredibly isolating. In the instant gratification and isolating world we live in, depression is debilitating. People who struggle with it are at a higher risk of death now than ever before.

#TheRealityOfDepressionIs that it's different for everyone. Advice, medication, and hotlines work for some but not others. If you don't have depression, reach out, give support, have compassion. If you have depression, do your best to find what helps you and accept that help.

If you're out there thinking that suicide is an inevitable part of your future, I'm here to tell you this: You can live through suicidal thoughts. You can live with depression. You can live. You may suffer a great deal. You may struggle through life. But you can live.

But each day, I find something to carry me through. Most of the time, I find people. Sometimes I find TV shows. Sometimes I find books. Sometimes I find my future. Sometimes I find myself. Whatever it is, I latch on and I let it push me through the worst moments.

I call my anxiety and depression "my darkness" because that's what it is. It swallows the color and light of the world. That color and light still exist, but not as it exists for everyone else. It's muted and distorted. On the worst days, they are dimmed completely.

So, if you're out there, and you're struggling with mental illness. Hang on. And don't be afraid to reach out. I know that last bit of advice is over-said, especially by people who aren't mentally ill, but reaching out saved my life time and time again. 11/13

It made me realize how bad my depression really was. I almost lost everything. I almost gave into the terrible thoughts. Now, I want to live and breathe and chase my dreams and love without a filter and be someone not weighed down by a mental health problem. 9/13

Nothing brought me joy or made me feel good. I was intentionally working far too many hours at my job because the only fulfillment I got was through work and it was only making things worse. I was hitting a wall. A bad one. And I was afraid I'd give into the thoughts. Soon. 5/13
